articles.title: French municipal elections: Socialists and LFI set aside differences to strike local deals
articles.content:
French municipal elections: Socialists and LFI set aside differences to strike local deals
After denouncing LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon's 'intolerable antisemitic remarks,' the Socialists allied with the radical left in key cities ahead of the runoff votes on Sunday.
France ready to join Strait of Hormuz ship escorts once situation 'calmer,' Macron says
The French president emphasized nevertheless that 'we are not a party to the conflict and therefore France will never take part in operations to open or liberate the Strait of Hormuz.'
Senior US counterterrorism official resigns to protest Iran war
In his resignation letter to Donald Trump, Joseph Kent said 'Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation, and it is clear that we started this war due to pressure from Israel and its powerful American lobby.'
UAE's fishermen are collateral victims of the war in Iran
Since the start of the war in Iran, fishing boats have been confined to ports along the Emirati coastline near the Strait of Hormuz. In Dubai, the sector has come to a standstill and fish market prices have soared.

Middle East
France rules out Hormuz ship escorts under 'bombings'
Speaking at a defense council meeting, Macron said France could help escort vessels in the strategic waterway, through which around 20% of global seaborne oil passes, but only after the situation has calmed down.
Published today at 7:57 pm (Paris) Le Monde with AFP
UAE's fishermen are collateral victims of the war in Iran
Since the start of the war in Iran, fishing boats have been confined to ports along the Emirati coastline near the Strait of Hormuz. In Dubai, the sector has come to a standstill and fish market prices have soared.
Published today at 6:42 pm (Paris), updated at 7:29 pm Philémon Barbier Isabelle Mandraud
France ready to join Strait of Hormuz ship escorts once situation 'calmer,' Macron says
The French president emphasized nevertheless that 'we are not a party to the conflict and therefore France will never take part in operations to open or liberate the Strait of Hormuz.'
Published today at 5:26 pm (Paris) Le Monde with AFP
Senior US counterterrorism official resigns to protest Iran war
In his resignation letter to Donald Trump, Joseph Kent said 'Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation, and it is clear that we started this war due to pressure from Israel and its powerful American lobby.'
Published today at 3:55 pm (Paris), updated at 3:56 pm Le Monde with AFP
Trump agitated and exasperated by continued blocking of strategic Strait of Hormuz
The US president criticized his European allies for their lack of enthusiasm after proposing an operation aimed at restoring freedom of navigation for oil tankers blocked in the Persian Gulf.
Published today at 12:45 pm (Paris) Gilles Paris
Israel says it killed Iran's security chief Ali Larijani in strike
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that he had been informed by Israel's military chief that Larijani and the head of Iran's Basij paramilitary force Gholamreza Soleimani 'were eliminated last night.'
Published today at 11:30 am (Paris), updated at 11:32 am Le Monde with AFP
'This is not our war': Europe refuses to be dragged into Trump's war with Iran
The American president has demanded that his allies help unblock the Strait of Hormuz for Gulf oil tankers. France aims to lead an international coalition to restore freedom of navigation, but only once hostilities have ended.
Published today at 10:20 am (Paris) Philippe Jacqué Elsa Conesa
In Iraqi Kurdistan, the trauma of the Halabja chemical massacre resurfaces as war returns to Iran
On March 16, 1988, Saddam Hussein's regime launched a mustard gas and sarin attack on the Kurdish town of Halabja, which at that time was suspected of collaborating with Iran, killing thousands. Thirty-eight years later, survivors remain haunted by those memories.
Published today at 2:56 am (Paris), updated at 10:02 am Nicolas Bourcier Pauline Gauer
'For Trump, the Middle East war is a way to avenge the United States' past military traumas'
Political scientist and US specialist Marie-Cécile Naves analyzes the narratives coming from the White House, highlighting a sensationalist war communications strategy that blurs the lines between fiction, reality and references from popular culture.
Published today at 1:11 am (Paris), updated at 9:48 am Marie-Cécile Naves
Baghdad's Green Zone targeted in drone attack
Air defenses foiled a rocket attack at the US embassy on Monday, and a drone sparked a fire on a luxury hotel. Iraq's interior ministry said there were no casualties or material damage.
Published yesterday at 11:53 pm (Paris), updated at 10:22 am Le Monde with AFP
Israel's president says Europe should back efforts to 'eradicate' Hezbollah
President Isaac Herzog said that the US-Iran war marked a 'historical juncture' and that it was in Europe's own national security interests to support his country's fight against Hezbollah. Lebanese authorities say that more than a million people have been displaced within the country during the past two weeks of fighting.
Published yesterday at 10:04 pm (Paris), updated at 7:44 am Le Monde with AFP
French court examines Yazidi genocide for first time in trial of jihadist
Sabri Essid is being tried in absentia, charged with 'genocide,' a first in France. Two women from the Iraqi minority will testify, recounting how they were enslaved.
Published yesterday at 12:55 pm (Paris), updated yesterday at 12:56 pm Soren Seelow
Trump says US is 'talking' to Iran, but it's not 'ready' for deal to end war
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran was not interested in talks with the US, pushing back on Trump's stance, though the US president insisted on Sunday that 'they want to make a deal badly.' Iran's supreme leader Ali Khameini and dozens of other Iranian officials died on the first day of the US-Israeli attacks on February 28.
Published yesterday at 3:09 am (Paris), updated yesterday at 4:49 am Le Monde with AFP
Macron tells Iran attacks on French interests 'unacceptable'
'I called on him to put an immediate end to the unacceptable attacks that Iran is carrying out against countries in the region, whether directly or through proxies, as in Lebanon and Iraq,' Macron said on X after his call with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Published yesterday at 1:47 am (Paris) Le Monde with AFP
War in Iran strains ammunition supplies, raising concern among military leadership
In just two weeks of war, Israeli and US forces have fired a record number of missiles to defend against Iranian attacks. As interceptor stocks like the Patriot dwindle, the race is on to replenish supplies.
Published on March 15, 2026, at 3:15 pm (Paris) Chloé Hoorman

Donald Trump asked world leaders on Saturday to send ships to the Strait of Hormuz to escort tankers.

Although the six Gulf countries have diversified their economies, hydrocarbons still account for about 30% of their gross domestic product (GDP). The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is also preventing them from importing goods, while the region relies on imports for 85% of its food supply.

Israel's dangerous calculations in Lebanon
